Here's some fun knowledge. In virtually all jurisdictions, there are two types of homicide that do not result in criminal penalties: Justified and Excused.

Excusable homicide is if you didn't mean to kill someone but they died because of a legally excusable action you took. This is the more common finding in many cases. For instance, you see someone shooting at a cop. To stop them, you run them down with your car and they die. This may be ruled excusable, as you did not necessarily intend for them to die, only to stop.

Justified homicide is when you intended to kill that motherfucker, you make no apologies for it and the court rules that yes, that motherfucker had to die. This finding is not as common. For instance, you find yourself standing behind an armed man with a hostage. You walk right up to that hostage and fire a round into the back of his head. You meant to kill, you wanted him to die at that moment so nothing worse would happen. Nothing about your actions indicated you wanted to give any chance of survival.

The interesting part here is that when a homicide is ruled justified, you are granted immunity from wrongful death civil suits. This is not the case with excusable homicides.

So next time you see a mother or family member tearfully crying on TV, look for a family attorney -- odds are they're planning to sue. You'll see this far less often with homicides ruled justified because there's no money to be had.
